description: Pre-authored sample questions for offline evaluation and zero-provider demo runs

questions.stem: What happens to the acceleration of an object when the net applied force doubles while mass remains constant?

distractor_map.Acceleration remains unchanged: Belief that acceleration depends strictly on mass alone
distractor_map.Acceleration is reduced by half: Inverting the direct relationship between force and acceleration
distractor_map.Acceleration is quadrupled: Confusing linear force proportionality with quadratic velocity scaling

questions.source_quote: If the net force acting on a constant mass is doubled, the resulting acceleration is doubled instantaneously.

questions.stem: A heavy horse pulls a wooden cart. By Newton's Third Law, the cart pulls back on the horse with equal force. Why does the cart still move forward?
options: The forward static friction force on the horse's hooves exceeds the cart's rolling resistance
The horse's pulling force is slightly greater than the cart's reaction force
Newton's third law applies only to objects at rest, not moving systems
The reaction force acts after a small time delay allowing forward motion
questions.correct_answer: The forward static friction force on the horse's hooves exceeds the cart's rolling resistance

distractor_map.The horse's pulling force is slightly gr: Belief that action must exceed reaction for acceleration to occur
distractor_map.Newton's third law applies only to objec: Belief that Newton's third law fails in dynamic motion
distractor_map.The reaction force acts after a small ti: Assuming a temporal lag in action-reaction pairs

questions.source_quote: These two forces act on different bodies and therefore never cancel each other out in single-body equilibrium calculations.

questions.stem: A box slides across a rough horizontal concrete floor and comes to rest. What is the sign of the work done by kinetic friction on the box?
options: Negative work, because friction acts opposite to the direction of displacement
Positive work, because friction transfers kinetic energy into the floor
Zero work, because friction is a non-conservative contact force
Positive work, because the total thermal energy of the system increases
questions.correct_answer: Negative work, because friction acts opposite to the direction of displacement

distractor_map.Positive work, because friction transfer: Confusing energy dissipation with positive mechanical work
distractor_map.Zero work, because friction is a non-con: Belief that non-conservative forces do zero mechanical work
distractor_map.Positive work, because the total thermal: Confusing thermodynamic heat generation with mechanical work sign

questions.source_quote: Kinetic friction acts opposite to the direction of relative displacement; hence the work done by kinetic friction is always negative

questions.stem: In an ideal mass-spring simple harmonic oscillator, at what position is the magnitude of acceleration at its maximum?
options: At the maximum displacement extreme points (x = +A and x = -A)
Halfway between equilibrium and maximum displacement (x = A/2)
Acceleration is constant throughout the entire oscillation cycle
questions.correct_answer: At the maximum displacement extreme points (x = +A and x = -A)

distractor_map.At the equilibrium midpoint (x = 0): Confusing maximum velocity with maximum acceleration
distractor_map.Halfway between equilibrium and maximum: Assuming acceleration peaks at intermediate displacement
distractor_map.Acceleration is constant throughout the: Believing SHM motion has uniform acceleration like free fall

questions.source_quote: At the extreme displacement points (x = +/- A), velocity is zero and acceleration is at its maximum magnitude.
